Goryu now ships as a Docker image, tells you in the log which link dropped and when, and can talk to a downstream that uses a different passphrase from your encoders.

## What's new

- **Docker image.** `docker run` it from `ghcr.io/live-miracles/goryu` or `nandisha0/goryu` (tags `3.4.0`, `3.4`, `latest`; linux/amd64). A compose file runs MediaMTX, Goryu and a bonded test sender, so you can watch two legs merge with no hardware: `docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml --profile demo up --build`.
- **Leg join and leave in the log.** A leg that drops or comes back used to leave no trace. Each change now logs one line, `Bonded leg left streamid=... leg=<ip>:<port> legs=1`, and the matching `joined` line, so the journal says which link failed and when. A flapping link is rate limited and summarised, not logged per flap.
- **A separate passphrase for the downstream.** The optional `output_passphrase` in `goryu.json` encrypts the connection to your server independently of the encoders' `passphrase`. Leave it out and nothing changes; set it to `""` for an unencrypted downstream on a trusted network.
- **Main/backup groups are tested and documented.** Broadcast groups were always supported; main/backup (a standby leg that takes over when the main leg fails) is now covered by the end-to-end tests, and the status API docs say what `idle` means.
- **Docs.** The README leads with the problem, and new pages cover [sending bonded SRT](https://github.com/live-miracles/goryu/blob/v3.4.0/docs/2-usage/2-sending-bonded-srt.md), [downstream servers](https://github.com/live-miracles/goryu/blob/v3.4.0/docs/2-usage/3-downstream-servers.md) (SRS, MediaMTX and datarhei Core tested) and [alternatives](https://github.com/live-miracles/goryu/blob/v3.4.0/docs/1-getting-started/3-alternatives.md).

## Upgrading

No breaking changes. The config and the status API are unchanged; `output_passphrase` and the new log lines are additions. Replace the binary (or pull the image) and restart; a restart drops active streams, so pick a quiet moment.

## Install

Download `goryu-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` below and check it against `checksums.sha256`, or:

```bash
docker run -d --name goryu --network host --restart unless-stopped \
  -v "$PWD/goryu.json:/etc/goryu/goryu.json:ro" nandisha0/goryu:3.4.0
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/live-miracles/goryu/compare/v3.3.0...v3.4.0
